claims.text: The initial eutectic HEA has a dual-phase microstructure containing a disordered FCC matrix and ordered B2 precipitates.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous elemental distribution and no grain-boundary segregation.
Intermediate thermal aging forms coherent, ordered B2 precipitates.
Intermediate thermal aging changes the density or degree of local chemical order within the B2 phase.
Raising the aging temperature changes FCC/B2 phase boundaries from coherent to semi-coherent or incoherent.
Atomic-size or lattice-parameter mismatch can generate friction that hinders dislocation motion and lowers ductility in an HEA.
Ordering within coherent B2 domains produces high lattice friction.
Ordered B2 domains impose an energy penalty on dislocations that shear them.
Coherent ordered B2 precipitates impede dislocation cross-slip.
Strong obstruction of dislocation motion by ordered B2 domains causes the transient dramatic loss of ductility.
At higher temperatures, thermal activation enables dislocations to bypass B2 domains by cross-slip or Orowan looping.
Loss of B2/FCC boundary coherency reduces lattice friction and restores ductility.
The alloy exhibits a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response correlated with B2 coherency and LCO density.
The ductile-brittle-ductile response occurs without corresponding changes in grain-boundary chemistry or grain size.
The baseline state has either no B2 phase or B2 with low coherency and low LCO density.

Embrittlement is confined to temperatures at which coherent B2 precipitates and maximal LCO density are present, below the onset of significant grain coarsening or grain-boundary impurity segregation.
The critical temperature for loss of B2 coherency and the critical LCO density are not quantified and may depend on alloy composition.
Observing brittleness without increased LCO density or coherent B2 precipitates would falsify the proposed mechanism.
Persistence of brittleness after B2 domains become incoherent, while grain boundaries remain chemically clean, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The material_initial_state specifies an existing ordered B2 phase, whereas the baseline permits the same initial state to have no B2 phase. The alternative low-coherency case is compatible, but the absent-B2 alternative is inconsistent with the stated dual-phase initial condition.

The mechanism describes ordered domains as difficult to shear and allows obstruction or bypass behavior, but the falsification rule requires dislocation shearing to be observed in the brittle state. Failure to observe shearing would not necessarily invalidate an obstacle mechanism based on resistance to shearing.
